messages:
rachel.o: Hi all  I had an urgent physio session in Dublin today for a shoulder strain. Clinic invoiced under my company member ID but when they tried to bill insurer it failed
nd they say the member ID on my digital card doesnt match their system. They want a paper ID card or an employer letter to proceed with direct billing. Im traveling and dont have the physical card. Can People Ops generate a one-page verification I can hand them? Also: if direct billing fails, what do I upload for reimbursement and how fast does that go?

leo.benefits: Sorry about that, hope your shoulder improves quickly. We can definitely generate a temporary verification letter with member name, member ID, plan code, and claims intake contact. That usually resolves mismatches at clinic front desks. We don't issue physical ID cards on the spot but we can include a screenshot of the digital card + the letter.

claims_bot: Automated claim guidance: For out-of-network or international outpatient care, submit at https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "International reimbursement". Required: itemized invoice (with CPT/code or service description), proof of payment (card receipt or bank stmt), date of service, attending provider name, and currency. Attach exchange rate evidence for reimbursement in different currency. Typical processing: 7-21 business days once full docs received; mark "urgent" for business travel or active work trips.

rachel.o: Clinic front desk specifically said their system flagged the member ID format (they have local prefixes). They asked for an employer letter that includes the member ID and the insurer's claim email so they can retry.

leo.benefits: I will include the insurer claim intake email and the insurer phone number in the letter. Copy you this exact paste for the desk to use when retrying billing:
```
Please submit invoice and patient details to: claims@redwood.com
Insurer phone (intl): +44-20-555-0199 (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 GMT)
Member ID: 012-345-678
Member name: Rachel O.
Plan: RW-PL-2039
```

fianna.claims: From claims side: if they retry and still fail, ask the clinic to email the invoice directly to claims@redwood.com with subject: "Invoice for Rachel O. - retry direct billing" and include their local provider ID. If they cannot direct bill, submit the invoice and proof of payment through the portal and include a short note "provider attempted direct billing". We'll flag for faster review.

conor.hr: If this was during a client visit, upload any calendar invite or client travel confirmation when you file and mention "business travel" to request expedited processing. Also, if youre worried about HSA eligibility, keep the itemized invoice and the physician note describing the diagnosis/treatment.

rachel.o: One more  clinic wants a scanned copy of my passport along with the employer letter for identity. Is that OK to provide?

leo.benefits: Yes, scanning your passport page is fine for the clinic billing verification. For privacy, hand the passport and ask them to scan or photocopy it themselves; you can also redact non-essential numbers if youre uncomfortable (but include name and DOB). Ill DM you the PDF letter now which includes the insurer contact and a short line in Irish English that might match their system phrasing.

claims_bot: System tip: for reimbursement include both the card statement entry showing the charge and the itemized receipt. If currency conversion is necessary, attach an OANDA screenshot for the date of service or your bank exchange record. If the provider emails claims@redwood.com directly, forward that email to leo.benefits so we can attach it to your claim file.

rachel.o: Got the DM letter and a screenshot of the digital card. Clinic accepted the PDF and will retry billing; they said they will email claims@redwood.com if it still fails. Thank you everyone for the quick help.

leo.benefits: Glad that helped. Follow up: if you end up paying and submitting for reimbursement, make sure the invoice includes the provider registration number (if available) and that you add "shoulder strain" or the treating diagnosis on upload for HSA substantiation. Ill mark the case as business travel and ask claims to expedite if we get the provider email.
